manual:
Clears registered run-scoped data after a game reset - a new game, BitNode destruction, augmentation install, or soft reset. It compares both augmentation and BitNode reset timestamps, then keeps a protected marker so it cannot confuse a normal dashboard restart with a reset. Current snapshots will normally self-heal on their next write, but history, running totals, and carry-over state would otherwise describe a run that no longer exists.

init/init.js invokes a disposable one-shot sweep before it starts Full Dashboard or Dashboard Lite, so File Shredder does not retain RAM as a persistent service. Its Options panel has a confirmed Run File Shredder control that force-clears registered files live; it does not restart the dashboard. Active services remain running and may republish their current telemetry on the next cycle, while protected dashboard options and deployment data are retained. The public dashboard contributes its own reset paths. Any separately installed source may add a JSON manifest under dashboard/reset-files/, so this service remains standalone while optional integrations clean up their own data. The Additional Reset Files option is only for a local run-scoped file whose owner has not yet supplied a manifest. Dashboard options, the deployment manifest, and File Shredder's own reset marker are always protected.
